title: Rust engine gets the HUD, pause menu, races and shadows
summary: A batch of Rust engine work is merged and live on the preview page /engine.html (deployment.json reports a3e7107): the in-ride HUD with the original speed meter, stunt text and GPS minimap, a keyboard help card, bundled desktop UI text, contact shadows and the High vehicle shadow map, tire tracks, the pause menu with settings screens, and single-player races with CPU riders. play.html is still the main JavaScript game.
details: HUD (#196): the shared Rust UI draws the original speed/preload meter and stunt text from Overlays.pb, a GPS minimap (terrain shading plus scenery triangles, north-up/heading-up tap toggle) and a keyboard help card with a Keys button. Against the JavaScript game over a flat backdrop (host Chromium, Apple M4, mean abs RGB /255): 1280x720 toolbar 0.47, minimap 0.95, card 0.74, meter 0.46, whole 0.18; 390x844 toolbar 0.10, minimap 0.95, card 1.40, meter 0.18. UI CPU 0.05-0.2 ms/frame; minimap build 27 ms against 58.8 ms in play.html. Not measured on physical phones.

Desktop text (#199): native text now picks faces by browser-style CSS font matching, fixing italic 800 falling back to the system face on macOS, and uses the bundled unmodified Fira Sans Condensed (SIL OFL 1.1) where Avenir Next Condensed is missing, as on Windows and Linux. The web build and live site fonts are unchanged.

Shadows and ground marks (#200, #201): contact shadows for Enhanced/High and a 2048 vehicle shadow map for High; tire tracks (Enhanced 600 segments / 15 s, High 3,600 / 75 s) and terrain anisotropy (Enhanced 4, High 16). ENV03 scripted-ride parity, Rust browser / native against JavaScript, mean abs /255: High 0.87 / 0.74 before shadows, 0.46 / 0.33 after #200, 0.16 / 0.04 after #201; Enhanced 0.17 / 0.04. Host CPU per frame at High: Chromium 0.79-1.20 ms, WebKit 1.36-2.31 ms, WebKit holding 60 Hz (host viewports, not phones).

Pause and settings (#202): the pause panel and its Settings, Display, Minimap, Race Overlays, Controls, Audio and Extras pages use the same rows as play.html and persist under play.html's own keys. Whole-viewport difference against the JavaScript menu over a flat backdrop: Minimap 3.05 (1280x720) / 4.94 (390x844), Extras 1.34 / 2.38; the JavaScript backdrop blur is not reproduced. Jukebox, Copy ride link, binding remapping and Alpha experiments rows are not in the Rust menu yet.

Races (#203): fury --race and /engine.html?race=1 load the course, pre-race shots, the original CPU roster (seeded) with each CPU's own quad and outfitted rider. ENV01, 1 lap, 3 CPUs, seed 12345: the Rust browser build matches the JavaScript game bit for bit (binary32) at every step for the player and all CPUs, over 1,800 steps of gas and 9,000 steps of a full race (player finishes first at step 7,213, 108.96 s). The native build follows the same phases but drifts from step 240 because desktop f32 math uses the system libm.
Pending: the speed-rush screen pass (#204) is open and not yet merged or deployed.
limitation: Preview page only; play.html remains the JavaScript game. Race overlays beyond the status line, race music and start-lamp sounds, crowd cues and flash bursts, fireworks, the drop gate and Restart/Quit menus are not connected. HUD gaps: card backdrop blur, race overlays/radar, remapped bindings in the card. Graphics, speed-rush, crash, flip, train and stats menu choices persist but the Rust ride does not apply them yet. Parity numbers are host measurements; nothing was measured on physical phones.
caption: Native desktop build (fury --race, 1280x720) on ENV01, the snow course: the player's ATV with three CPU riders on their own quads in the scripted parity race, a frame captured after the start (scripted run labelled 800). The status line and race overlays are not drawn in this capture and are not yet ported.
